# Toward a persistent event-streaming system for high-performance computing applications

**2025 · DOI: 10.3389/fhpcp.2025.1638203 · OpenAlex: W4414299303**
*Matthieu Dorier, Amal Gueroudji, Valérie Hayot-Sasson, Hai Duc Nguyen, Seth Ockerman et al.*

## What this folder is

This is a citation-impact analysis of the paper above, produced by [wake](https://github.com/rbross-hpc/wake). It catalogs every work that cites this paper, classifies the *nature* of each citation (does the citing work extend it, use it as a tool, benchmark against it, or just mention it in passing?), and — for the highest-signal citations — reads the full text of the citing paper to verify that classification and quote the specific passages that support it.

## What was done

- **4** citing works pulled from OpenAlex
- **4** classified by an LLM from title/abstract into one of seven relationship types (extends, builds-on, uses-as-tool, benchmarks, applies-to-domain, related-infrastructure, background-mention)
- **2** had their full PDF fetched, extracted, and re-classified against the actual body text, with supporting passages quoted directly
- **2** verified findings signed off by a human reviewer
- **0** confirmed (2 still draft) combined-evidence theme(s) synthesized across multiple dossiers
- a narrative assembled from those confirmed themes

## Where to start

- **Get the top-line finding fast** — read the [Impact Brief](impact.md). Its "Strongest Evidence" section ranks the most impactful adoptions.
- **Read the story** — read the [Narrative](narrative.md), prose that stitches the confirmed themes together with numbered citations back to the evidence.
- **Drill into a specific citing work** — start at the [Evidence Wiki](evidence/index.md) and pick a dossier. Each has quoted passages with page numbers.
- **See what patterns emerged across citing works** — read [Themes](evidence/themes/index.md).
- **Audit what was investigated, in what order** — read the [Log](evidence/log.md).

## Reading conventions

- Every `.md` file in this folder that documents a specific finding has a `.json` sidecar with the same data in structured form. The `.md` is what you're meant to read; the `.json` is for tools.
- "Provisional" findings are from the abstract only — treat them as placeholder guesses. "Verified" findings have been checked against the full text and signed off by a human.
- All links in this folder are relative, so the whole folder can be moved, zipped, or shared and everything will still resolve.
- A citing work flagged as author-overlap with the seed is the seed's own team publishing follow-on work, not independent third-party adoption — called out wherever it applies.

## Editing this folder by hand

Human-facing files you might edit directly, one JSON object per line:

- `overrides.jsonl` — record a corrected classification
- `duplicates.jsonl` — mark a citing work as a duplicate of another
- `exclusions.jsonl` — exclude a work from theme synthesis
- `manual_abstracts.jsonl` — supply an abstract OpenAlex is missing

These are append-only — later lines for the same work win, nothing is ever rewritten in place. Everything else in this folder is derived from these plus the raw fetched/LLM data, and is safe to delete and regenerate.
